mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative when GDP is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are positive when unemployment rises.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate coupled with low unemployment indicates tight monetary policy, negatively impacting S&P 500 over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive under high rates and low unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate in a tightening cycle leads to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when rates rise above 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production suggests strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative when production increases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts indicate strong demand, but may lead to inflation, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when housing starts increase.

mechanism_narrative: High retail sales (RSAFS) and low federal funds rate indicate strong demand and easy money, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative with high RSAFS and low FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing payroll employment in an expansion regime signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are negative when payroll employment increases.
